plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs that burst into rose-like blooms with layered satin petals and golden centers. They bring bright color to the quiet depths of winter gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with peak bloom in midwinter
plants.location: Japan, and mild-winter gardens in the southeastern United States and western Europe
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed to make a prized culinary and cosmetic oil in Japan.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A wide, umbrella-shaped tree that becomes a canopy of fiery blossoms. Ruffled petals, one of them streaked with white, hang above feathery fern-like leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere, roughly November through February
plants.location: Northern Australia and other southern tropical and subtropical regions
plants.funFact: Although the tree is a favorite across the tropics, it is endangered in its native Madagascar.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A tough, shade-loving perennial that opens nodding, saucer-shaped white flowers with golden stamens. It often blooms while frost and snow still cover the ground.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring, often starting around December
plants.location: Woodlands of the Alps and gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, the Christmas rose is not a true rose. It belongs to the buttercup family and is toxic if eaten.
